subject.title: [Feature]: Add provider-profile routing policies for multi-account OAuth/API pools (starting with google-gemini-cli)

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in provider-profile pool routing contract for batch/worker workloads, and what minimal public config/state surface should it expose first?
rationale: The remaining work changes public config, persisted auth state, provider fallback semantics, status/probe output, and upgrade behavior; automation should not invent those product boundaries or defaults.

options.title: Design additive core pool routing
options.body: Define a minimal opt-in provider/auth pool routing contract that preserves current session-sticky defaults and starts with one observable strategy before expanding to quota, bucket, and weighting semantics.

options.title: Keep this as phased tracker
options.body: Use this issue as the canonical umbrella while keeping key-bucket, rotation-depth, and pace-governance work as narrower linked acceptance criteria.

options.title: Defer to external/plugin surfaces
options.body: Keep current core behavior and recommend sidecars or future plugin/provider hooks until maintainers decide native config/state complexity is justified.

recommendation.title: Design additive core pool routing
recommendation.body: Define a minimal opt-in provider/auth pool routing contract that preserves current session-sticky defaults and starts with one observable strategy before expanding to quota, bucket, and weighting semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses auth config, persisted state, provider routing, docs, and compatibility policy, and steipete has the strongest recent history on those boundaries.
